crossSourceRelationship.basis: The full publisher-hosted 2009 article was reviewed through its official PDF text view. Three authors overlap, both works name the same five Nueva Ecija waters, both describe three stations and ten 10 m by 12 m quadrats per Nueva Ecija study area, and both discuss overlapping fish-name leads.
crossSourceRelationship.additional2009Scope: The Silliman article also covers Pampanga River reaches in Apalit, San Simon, and San Luis and Candaba Swamp.
crossSourceRelationship.lineageAssessment: The shared authors, exact Nueva Ecija site list, matching field design, and repeated fish-name leads indicate a close study lineage, possibly a reanalysis or extension. Neither reviewed source establishes dataset independence or gives the fish collection dates needed to distinguish independent fieldwork.
crossSourceRelationship.unresolved: Do not sum the 2006 and 2009 richness totals or treat them as independent survey confirmations. Visually verify the 2009 table cells and seek its underlying field log or 2005 CLSU source before building a site-by-site fish candidate matrix.

limits: This proceedings item is a short abstract, not a species-by-site data table.
No field sampling dates, station coordinates, vouchers, or site-level fish labels are given in the reviewed pages.
The four native/endemic and seven introduced fish totals are study-wide aggregates; they cannot be assigned to a specific river or lake.
The source's historical labels are recorded as printed and are not silently normalized to current accepted names.
No item-specific open reuse license was identified. The review retains only short attributed summaries and does not reproduce tables or figures.
nextStep: The official 2009 full text is now browser-readable and reviewed.
